what: The aggregated breaking-wave statistics and the analysis scripts of Guimarães, Stringari, Leckler, Ardhuin — Geometry of breaking waves at natural sea (Zenodo, 2026-01-29, CC-BY-4.0): the seven files under codes/ of an 8.9 GB archive whose remaining 145,050 entries are per-event .mat files and .png frames. Extracted here WITHOUT downloading the archive: its ZIP64 central directory (28.6 MB at offset 8,883,533,609) was read by HTTP range request and each entry fetched by its own range and inflated. Every extracted file hashes below; the archive itself is pinned by the md5 Zenodo publishes.
note: blacksea_data.pkl is a pandas DataFrame pickle (the scripts read it with pickle.load); it was converted ONCE to blacksea_data.csv, whose literals round-trip every double exactly, and the CSV is what instruments/breaking reads. Columns and definitions in claims.json. Menu item 5 of notes/ufsc-labeco-menu-2026-09-12.md.

blacksea_data.csv.how: written from blacksea_data.pkl by pandas 3.0.5 in a scratch venv: every double as its shortest round-tripping decimal (Python repr), verified column by column against the pickle with float_precision=round_trip; the pickle is the archive's bytes, the CSV is THE RECORD the instrument reads

claims.json.how: the claims the ledger reads: the record's description and the reference lines the scripts draw; transcribed by hand

paper.how: the publisher's full-text XML (doi/full-xml), fetched in a headed Chrome because the host refuses headless and curl; pinned as the text the numbers are read from
